declared_parity.parity_note: AGENT-PIXEL PARITY (supersample 2, against MuJoCo at its default offsamples=4, 25 cells x 64 states). Every disagreement is inside the agent's own silhouette: the baked plate is exact by construction, non-agent pixels are 99.88-99.99% bit-identical, and that residual is the reference's multisampling bleeding agent colour into neighbouring wall/floor pixels. On agent-interior pixels (eroded by one, so coverage is not in play) the shader reaches 48-84% within 1/255 for pointmaze (mean 1.2-2.5/255), 0-51% for antmaze and 0-3% for humanoidmaze. The legged numbers are not a shading result: at the official whole-maze camera the ant is 12-70 px and the humanoid 4-21 px of 50176, and eroding leaves as few as 1 interior pixel, so their agreement is a statement about a silhouette under the reference's coverage rule. Against a NON-multisampled reference the same shader reaches 92.4% within 1/255 over 13,069 pooled agent-interior pixels (mean 0.88/255), which localises most of the remaining gap in MSAA sample positions -- GPU-specific, not recoverable by fitting -- rather than in shading. Three mechanisms were tried and are recorded so they are not retried: the fixed-function composition (FIXED - specular is additive and white and the texture modulates the whole primary colour, which took wall tops from 13/255 worst to 2/255 and made vertical wall faces bit-exact); Gouraud interpolation over MuJoCo's sphere/capsule tessellation (REFUTED - ten (slices, stacks, phase, diagonal) variants all scored 0.0-0.2% exact against 1.6% for plain per-pixel, which is also what sub-pixel triangles predict); and a mis-shaped specular lobe (REFUTED - a 24-knot piecewise-linear lobe fitted under four light/specular geometries, headlight directional or point crossed with Blinn or Phong, could not explain floor and agent with one curve).

declared_parity.parity_note: parity_interior_min is NOT relaxed: interior-pixel agreement measures exactly 1.000000 -- 0 bad pixels out of 9,834,291 -- over 201 independent draws of 64 states at the shipped default_supersample = 1. What is declared is parity_all_exact_min, and the reason is arithmetic rather than a tolerance -- all-pixel exactness is interior exactness WEIGHTED BY HOW MUCH OF THE FRAME MOVES, and finger-turn_easy's seven movers cover 11.7% of an 84 px frame against cartpole's 2.5%. Measured over those 201 draws: all-pixel 0.9103 at WORST and 0.9119 median, i.e. it CLEARS the shared 0.90 bar on every draw -- the floor is declared so that the margin is the scene's rather than luck's, and it is set from a draw count rather than from one large evaluation, because a rare pixel event reported off a single draw is how MujocoPusher came to declare a floor it then failed 15 times in 101. 100.0% of every disagreeing pixel is inside the ray-cast mover pass and the baked plate is 1.00000 exact on the pixels it owns; the residual is a one-level rim on curved silhouettes, where MuJoCo shades a tessellated capsule per vertex and an analytic per-pixel evaluation lands within a few levels of it. finger-spin (0.9288 worst) and finger-turn_hard (0.9241 worst) are the same renderer with fewer mover pixels and declare nothing. Dropping the supersample IMPROVED all three -- at ss=2 the same draws gave 0.9053 / 0.9249 / 0.9200 -- because an aliased edge is bit-identical to MuJoCo wherever MuJoCo's own MSAA happened to be fully covered, while a blended edge almost never is.

render_parity_with_official_renderer.bound_from: the env's own declaration, defaulting to tests/gpu/test_conformance.py:INTERIOR_EXACT_MIN

declared_parity.parity_note: AGENT-PIXEL PARITY (supersample 2, against MuJoCo at its default offsamples=4, 25 cells x 64 states). Every disagreement is inside the agent's own silhouette: the baked plate is exact by construction, non-agent pixels are 99.88-99.99% bit-identical, and that residual is the reference's multisampling bleeding agent colour into neighbouring wall/floor pixels. On agent-interior pixels (eroded by one, so coverage is not in play) the shader reaches 48-84% within 1/255 for pointmaze (mean 1.2-2.5/255), 0-51% for antmaze and 0-3% for humanoidmaze. The legged numbers are not a shading result: at the official whole-maze camera the ant is 12-70 px and the humanoid 4-21 px of 50176, and eroding leaves as few as 1 interior pixel, so their agreement is a statement about a silhouette under the reference's coverage rule. Against a NON-multisampled reference the same shader reaches 92.4% within 1/255 over 13,069 pooled agent-interior pixels (mean 0.88/255), which localises most of the remaining gap in MSAA sample positions -- GPU-specific, not recoverable by fitting -- rather than in shading. Three mechanisms were tried and are recorded so they are not retried: the fixed-function composition (FIXED - specular is additive and white and the texture modulates the whole primary colour, which took wall tops from 13/255 worst to 2/255 and made vertical wall faces bit-exact); Gouraud interpolation over MuJoCo's sphere/capsule tessellation (REFUTED - ten (slices, stacks, phase, diagonal) variants all scored 0.0-0.2% exact against 1.6% for plain per-pixel, which is also what sub-pixel triangles predict); and a mis-shaped specular lobe (REFUTED - a 24-knot piecewise-linear lobe fitted under four light/specular geometries, headlight directional or point crossed with Blinn or Phong, could not explain floor and agent with one curve).

declared_parity.parity_note: 1 ulp of exp, not geometry. Run on the CPU with the reference's own float32 exp this renderer reproduces the official frame BIT FOR BIT and the device contributes nothing (measured both ways); the residual is entirely that our exp is correctly rounded and torch's CPU float32 exp is only faithful. That ulp changes a pixel only where the dot's colour equals the background, because 255*(1-a)+255*a is the identity in exact arithmetic and not in float32, and the 41 px Gaussian tail is flat enough that the reference's own 3x3 neighbourhood cannot see the quantisation contour. Worst of 800 seeded draws: 2 pixels of 2.3 million, 1/255, one channel. See the module docstring.

declared_parity.parity_note: 1 ulp of exp, not geometry. Run on the CPU with the reference's own float32 exp this renderer reproduces the official frame BIT FOR BIT and the device contributes nothing (measured both ways); the residual is entirely that our exp is correctly rounded and torch's CPU float32 exp is only faithful. That ulp changes a pixel only where the dot's colour equals the background, because 255*(1-a)+255*a is the identity in exact arithmetic and not in float32, and the 41 px Gaussian tail is flat enough that the reference's own 3x3 neighbourhood cannot see the quantisation contour. Worst of 800 seeded draws: 2 pixels of 2.3 million, 1/255, one channel. See the module docstring.
